boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Rollins traditions, from first-year welcome rituals to the surprise appearance of the Fox.

cards.title: Serve on SPARC Day
cards.subtitle: New-student orientation tradition
cards.notes: Join the orientation day of service, then use the reflection time to connect the project with the Winter Park community.
cards.short_summary: First-years volunteer with local organizations as part of orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies SPARC Day as an annual orientation tradition in which first-year students volunteer with dozens of local organizations and reflect on their impact.
cards.access_notes: Orientation programming for new Rollins students; confirm participation details with Student Affairs.

cards.title: Raise a Candle at Candlewish
cards.subtitle: Fall-semester first-year gathering
cards.notes: Bring your first-year intentions to the fall gathering and take part when the group raises candles around the Fiat Lux theme.
cards.short_summary: A candle-raising welcome ritual centered on community, learning, and Rollins’ motto.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins says first-years gather at the start of each fall semester, receive candles, and raise them to symbolize community, knowledge, and “Fiat Lux.”
cards.access_notes: Held during fall welcome programming for first-year students; check orientation communications for details.

cards.title: Wait for Fox Day
cards.subtitle: Surprise spring academic holiday
cards.notes: Watch for the president’s spring announcement; when the Fox appears, pause class plans and join the campus programming.
cards.short_summary: A surprise day off triggered by the president’s placement of the Fox statue.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins states that Fox Day was established in 1956 and that the president cancels College of Liberal Arts classes on a surprise spring day.
cards.access_notes: Applies to College of Liberal Arts classes on the day selected by the president; programming is announced that day.

cards.title: Spot the Fox on Tars Plaza
cards.subtitle: Fox Day signal at Tars Plaza
cards.notes: Check Tars Plaza on likely spring mornings and photograph the moment only after the president places the Fox statue there.
cards.short_summary: The statue’s appearance is the visual signal that Fox Day has arrived.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins says the president places the Fox statue on Tars Plaza early in the morning to signal Fox Day.
cards.access_notes: The statue is placed only on Fox Day; do not handle or move it.

cards.title: Pick Up a Fox Day Proclamation
cards.subtitle: President’s office, Fox Day morning
cards.notes: If you are on campus when Fox Day begins, line up outside the president’s office for the day’s proclamation and a donut.
cards.short_summary: The president hands out printed Fox Day proclamations as the celebration starts.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins documents that, on Fox Day, the president hands out Fox Day proclamations and donuts to students lined up outside the president’s office.
cards.access_notes: Available only on Fox Day and while supplies last; follow on-site directions.

cards.title: Enter the Lip Sync Challenge
cards.subtitle: SGA-connected student-group performance
cards.notes: Form a student-group team, plan a lip-sync-and-dance routine, and follow the event organizer’s participation and audience guidance.
cards.short_summary: Student groups perform choreographed lip-sync and dance routines before a campus audience.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins describes Lip Sync as an annual lip-sync and dance challenge in which dozens of student groups participate.
cards.access_notes: Participation and viewing details are set by the Student Government Association for each event.

cards.title: Take a Finals-Eve Breakfast Break
cards.subtitle: Skillman Dining Hall, eve of finals
cards.notes: On the eve of finals, stop by Skillman for the breakfast event and a study break served by faculty, staff, and the president.
cards.short_summary: A free finals-eve breakfast event staffed by Rollins faculty and leaders.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins calls Late Night Breakfast a free eve-of-finals event at Skillman Dining Hall where faculty, staff, and the president serve breakfast foods.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled on the eve of finals each semester; confirm event timing and eligibility through campus announcements.

cards.entity_name: Thaddeus & Polly Seymour Acts of Kindness Day
cards.title: Mark Acts of Kindness Day
cards.subtitle: Annual February service tradition
cards.notes: Use the February observance to organize a practical act of service for a neighbor, campus group, or Winter Park community partner.
cards.short_summary: A February day of service honoring Thaddeus and Polly Seymour’s legacy.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins says that since 2020 it has honored Thaddeus and Polly Seymour each February with an annual day for service and commitment to the community.
cards.access_notes: Look for February service opportunities announced by Rollins; activity locations vary.

cards.title: Attend Christmas Vespers
cards.subtitle: Knowles Memorial Chapel holiday service
cards.notes: Reserve a ticket for the annual candlelit program of carols and lessons, then arrive through the Chapel’s published entry process.
cards.short_summary: A candlelit Rollins holiday service with a history dating to 1933.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins identifies Christmas Vespers as an annual candlelit College tradition with a history stretching back to 1933.
cards.access_notes: The published event page lists ticketed admission; Rollins students, faculty, and staff receive complimentary tickets by reservation.

cards.title: Try the Pancake Flip
cards.subtitle: Mills Lawn, orientation week
cards.notes: During orientation week, meet on Mills Lawn and try catching pancakes with fellow new Tars as the event is offered.
cards.short_summary: An orientation-week Mills Lawn activity where new students try to catch pancakes.
cards.evidence_claim: Rollins describes the annual Pancake Flip on Mills Lawn during orientation week as a Rollins tradition for new Tars.
cards.source_title: Rollins College: A Year in Photos
cards.access_notes: An orientation-week activity for new students; availability and timing should be confirmed in the current orientation schedule.
